13741105_cc00f279.text: the thalamus also contains "inhibitory nuclei" that are exclusively composed of GABAergic neurons, which include the intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) and ventral lateral geniculate (vLG) nucleus. Notably, recent studies identified a small progenitor domain (rostral thalamic progenitor [pTH-R] domain) that is located rostral to the caudal thalamic progenitor (pTH-C) domain during neurogenesis and expresses the proneural bHLH factors ASCL1 and TAL1. Population-level fate-mapping studies using these markers found that pTH-R contributes to IGL and vLG nuclei (Fig 1A; [3]4]).
